import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 520

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/520](https://www.erdosproblems.com/520)
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Nat Real Filter

namespace Erdos520

variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]

/--
A random function $f$ is Rademacher multiplicative if $f(1) = 1$,
for each prime $p$, we independently choose $f(p) \in \{-1, 1\}$ uniformly at random (so each
$f(p)$ is a measurable function of the sample point),
for each square-free integer $n = p_1 \cdots p_r$, $f(n) = f(p_1) \cdots f(p_r)$, and
for each non-squarefree integer $n$, $f(n) = 0$.
-/
structure IsRademacherMultiplicative (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) : Prop where
  /-- Prime entries are random variables. -/
  measurable_of_prime p : p.Prime → Measurable (f p)
  /-- Prime entries are independent. -/
  iIndepFun_primes : iIndepFun (fun p : Primes ↦ f p) ℙ
  /-- Primes entries are uniformly distributed on `{-1, 1}`. -/
  prob_of_prime p : p.Prime → ℙ {ω | f p ω = 1} = 1 / 2 ∧ ℙ {ω | f p ω = -1} = 1 / 2
  map_one ω : f 1 ω = 1
  map_mul_of_coprime a b ω : a.Coprime b → f (a * b) ω = f a ω * f b ω
  map_of_not_squarefree n ω : ¬ Squarefree n → f n ω = 0

/--
Let $f$ be a Rademacher multiplicative function.
Does there exist some constant $c > 0$ such that, almost surely,
$$
  \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{m \leq N} f(m)}{\sqrt{N \log \log N}} = c?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 60]
theorem erdos_520 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ (Ω : Type) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
      (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), IsRademacherMultiplicative f →
      ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun N ↦ ∑ m ≤ N, f m ω / sqrt (N * log (log N))) atTop = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos520

status_issues.source_status: Newer primary literature gives a negative answer: Durkan and Pearce-Crump's Theorem 1 (v1 submitted 31 July 2026) proves the almost-sure bound |Σ_{n≤x} f(n)| ≪_{ε,f} √x (log log x)^(1/4+ε). Verreault independently proves a stronger bound (v1 submitted 21 August 2026) and explicitly recognizes the independent result. The cited problem website and its public data still label 520 OPEN; this flag is based on the newer papers, not a changed website label.
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2607.29429v1, Theorem 1; https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.21354v1, introduction and first corollary. Taking ε=1/8 in the former bounds the absolute value of the source's normalized sum by C_f (log log N)^(-1/8), which tends to zero. Consequently its limsup is zero, not a positive constant.
status_issues.suggested_change: Confirm acceptance of these recent preprints, then change the category to research solved and the answer to answer(False), adding the new references. Leave the mathematical right-hand side unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses real-valued random variables with probability conditions for the prime signs and coprime-multiplicativity axioms, rather than a literally {-1,0,1}-valued prime-product construction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The measurable events f(p)=1 and f(p)=-1 are disjoint and have total probability one. Countability of the primes gives a common full-measure set on which every prime value is a sign. The algebraic fields are equivalent to f(n)=∏_{p∣n} f(p) for squarefree n and zero otherwise, including f(1)=1 and f(0)=0. Replacing prime values on the exceptional null set by signs and extending by this formula gives the source's literal model without changing the almost-sure conclusion. Conversely, the source construction satisfies the Lean fields. The algebraic equivalence and simultaneous almost-sure prime support were proved in scratch; the complete null-set-modification equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The limsup is real-valued without explicit boundedness assumptions. The natural-number sum includes zero and divides each summand by the normalization.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A real limsup defaults to zero when the required boundedness or coboundedness fails. Since c>0, equality to c excludes both cases and is equivalent to the extended-real limsup being the finite value c. Also, the definition forces f(0)=0, and Finset.sum_div exactly factors out the common denominator. Scratch proves the displayed expression equivalent to the EReal limsup of the normalized sum over Icc 1 N. The denominator's zero values at N=0,1,2 affect only a finite prefix; it is positive for N≥3.

reformulations.difference: One constant c is quantified uniformly over every probability space and every realization satisfying IsRademacherMultiplicative, whereas the source speaks of a Rademacher multiplicative function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every such prime family has the same joint law: the countable product of fair sign distributions. Every other entry is determined by finite prime products, so the complete sequence and its measurable limsup event have the same law in every realization. Thus a constant valid almost surely in the canonical product model works for all models. Conversely, the universal statement applies to that canonical model.
